name: Restorative Campus Spaces at Southeast University (PRS-11 Panoramas)
description:
Method replication: same task, scale and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (88 Baidu street views re-fetched on and around the Jiulonghu campus of Southeast University, Nanjing, 2015–2022; like the paper, each is four views at 90° field of view and 20° upward pitch, front, right, rear and left, joined into one strip).

Original study: Wu, Lin, Chen & Wu (2025), Land 14(3), 610. Panoramas of the Jiulonghu campus were stitched from four Baidu Map API views. In an online survey (15 September to 15 October 2024), 670 respondents each got five randomly assigned panoramas, one per page, imagined themselves in the scene and scored the 11 PRS-11 statements (being away, fascination, coherence, scope) from 1 to 7. 3,350 records over 250 scenes gave restorative benefit scores used to train an XGBoost model for the whole campus, combined with sDNA accessibility.

Differences from the original study: (1) 88 new panoramas instead of the paper's 250; the sampling box also covers some campus edges, and the views are from Baidu's 2015–2022 captures, not August 2024. (2) The five panoramas are drawn at random for each participant; the paper balanced how often each scene appeared. (3) PRS-11 wording follows Pasini et al. (2014) in English; the paper's Chinese wording is not printed. (4) The questions about the participant (gender, age, university role, knowing the campus) are ours. (5) The paper's 118 on-site campus questionnaires are not part of this template.
author: Wu, Lin, Chen & Wu

config.description: Participants see 5 random Baidu street-view panoramas of the Jiulonghu campus of Southeast University (Nanjing) and rate each on the 11 PRS-11 statements from 1 to 7. Restorative benefit = mean of the 11 items. Method replication of Wu, Lin, Chen & Wu (2025), Land 14(3): 610.
